climate.overview_html: The 2026 Super El Niño remains the dominant climate signal of the week, with WMO confirming Niño 3.4 at +3.34°C on 6 October and projecting +3.7°C for October–December — well above the prior record of +2.6°C from November 2015. IPCC-65 opened this morning (12 October) in Addis Ababa for a sixth consecutive attempt to resolve the AR7 delivery-timeline deadlock; the COP31 co-presidency has scheduled a virtual consultation with IPCC delegates for 14 October, four weeks before COP31 opens in Antalya. Fossil-fuel phase-out language, climate finance, and the 1.5°C framing remain the main COP31 fault lines, with the EU insisting there is “no scope” for new finance pledges and small island states pushing hard for a Pacific high-level session. A new Nature Geoscience study (Kopp et al.) confirms Antarctic ice loss is “very likely” on all 2100 emissions pathways, yet highest-ambition cuts still halve the upper-end sea-level contribution.

items.headline: WMO October 2026 El Niño Update: Niño 3.4 Observed +3.34°C (6 Oct), Projected +3.7°C Peak December — Would Be Strongest on Record; Central Pacific Exceeds 30°C for First Time; Near-100% Probability Through February 2027
items.summary: The WMO Global Seasonal Climate Update (October 7–8, 2026) reports the Niño 3.4 anomaly reached +3.34°C on October 6 and is projected to average approximately +3.7°C for October–December 2026, peaking around December — far above the prior record of +2.6°C from the November 2015–January 2016 event. The central Pacific exceeded 30°C (86°F) for the first time in records. WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo stated there is near-100% probability the event will persist through February 2027, potentially ranking among the strongest since at least 1950. A positive Indian Ocean Dipole is expected to peak in October before declining. The consensus of 13 national and international centres underpins these projections. Strong El Niño events often coincide with record-warm global years; WMO warns of compound drought and flood anomalies across Australasia, southern Africa, South America and South Asia through northern spring 2027.

items.headline: IPCC-65 Now Underway in Addis Ababa (12–16 October): AR7 Timeline Deadlocked Sixth Consecutive Session; COP31 Presidency Schedules 14 October Virtual Consultation; Trust Fund at Risk by End-2028
items.summary: IPCC-65 opened on Monday October 12 at the Ethiopian Meteorological Institute in Addis Ababa, running through October 16. The primary agenda item is the AR7 delivery timeline, unresolved across five consecutive prior sessions. The key division: one bloc (EU and small island states) presses for all three Working Group reports by July–September 2028 to inform the 2028 Global Stocktake; a second bloc (including major emerging economies) seeks WG2 and WG3 deferred to mid-2029. IPCC Chair Sir Jim Skea described the prior session outcome as ‘frustrating and disappointing’ with ‘minimal outcomes.’ Summaries from sessions 61–63 also remain unapproved. The IPCC Secretariat has warned its trust fund will be exhausted by end-2028 without new contributions. COP31 co-presidency (Turkey/Australia) has scheduled a virtual consultation with IPCC delegates for October 14 to coordinate the AR7 timeline with the COP31 preparation process.

items.headline: COP31 Co-Presidency Circulates Draft Cover Decision Text; Türkiye and Australia Seek “Ambitious” Action Language; 1.5°C Framing, Fossil Fuel Phase-Out and Finance Pledges Remain Contested
items.summary: Turkey and Australia circulated draft COP31 cover decision text on October 8, 2026, building on the Fiji Pre-COP framework announced the prior day. The co-presidency framing aims for ‘ambitious’ action language adopted by consensus at Antalya without line-by-line negotiation. Key fault lines: whether the text explicitly acknowledges 1.5°C overshoot risk; what language — if any — it carries on fossil fuel phase-out; and how it treats new finance pledges versus implementation of existing commitments. COP31 co-president Turkey’s Murat Kurum called 1.5°C ‘a matter of survival’ for the Pacific at the Fiji pre-COP. Euronews reports that Turkey frames COP31 as an ‘implementation COP’ focused on delivering existing commitments rather than announcing new targets.

items.headline: 2026 Arctic Sea Ice Minimum: 4.6 Million km² on 12 September — Tied 10th Lowest in 47 Years; All 20 Lowest Satellite-Era Summer Minima Occurred During 2007–2026
items.summary: NASA and NSIDC confirmed the 2026 Arctic sea ice minimum at approximately 4.6 million km² on September 12, tying 2008, 2010 and 2025 for the 10th lowest in 47 years of satellite observations — 1.21 million km² above the 2012 all-time record low. All 20 lowest Arctic summer minima in the satellite record have now occurred in the last 20 years (2007–2026). NSIDC notes no statistically significant further long-term decline in September minimum extent over the post-2007 low plateau; rather, the pattern reflects a roughly stable record-low regime established since the 2007 step-change, with the 2026 Super El Niño warm SST environment potentially adding to late-season melt.

items.headline: Nature Geoscience (Kopp et al.): Antarctic Ice Loss “Very Likely” on All 2100 Emissions Pathways; Highest-Ambition Paris Pathway Reduces Upper-End Antarctic SLR by ~50% vs. Very High Emissions; 95th Percentile Very High Emissions: 25.4 cm
items.summary: A Nature Geoscience study led by Rutgers climate scientist Robert Kopp finds Antarctic ice loss contributing to global sea-level rise by 2100 is ‘very likely’ under all studied emissions scenarios. Under very high emissions, the 95th-percentile Antarctic sea-level contribution reaches 25.4 cm by 2100 (median 15.7 cm). The highest-ambition Paris-consistent pathway carries at least 89% probability of producing less Antarctic ice loss by century’s end. The authors emphasise that near-term emissions choices still meaningfully bound long-term Antarctic sea-level risk, despite committed ice loss being unavoidable on all pathways.

items.headline: EU Finalises COP31 Negotiating Position: Mitigation Work Programme to 2040; 2028 Global Stocktake Mechanism; “No Scope” for New Finance Pledges; Position Cites UNEP Finding 1.5°C to Be Exceeded
items.summary: The EU finalised its COP31 negotiating position on October 6, calling for extending the Mitigation Work Programme to at least 2040, establishing a mechanism for the 2028 Global Stocktake, and implementing existing commitments rather than making new finance pledges — the draft states there is ‘no scope’ for additional pledges at COP31. The position directly cites the UNEP Limiting Overshoot report, which concluded 1.5°C will likely be exceeded within a few years and that the most stringent Paris pathways ‘are no longer feasible.’

items.headline: Pacific Resilience Facility Reaches ~$200 Million After $15 Million Pre-COP Pledges From Fiji, Ireland, Netherlands and Denmark; $500 Million COP31 Target Remains Far Off; Delegates Visit Tuvalu Land Reclamation
items.summary: Nations including Fiji, Ireland, the Netherlands and Denmark pledged approximately $15 million to the Pacific Resilience Facility on October 7, raising the total to just under $200 million. Roughly half has come from Pacific island governments, New Zealand and Australia. The PRF targets $500 million after COP31 and $1.5 billion long-term. Delegates were taken to Tuvalu to witness land being created from dredged sand in response to sea-level rise — a direct demonstration of frontline climate adaptation.

major_events.name: Hurricane Simon (Eastern Pacific) — CATEGORY 3 (DOWN FROM CAT-4 PEAK 155 MPH); THREATENING MEXICO’S PACIFIC COAST; JALISCO, COLIMA, NAYARIT, MICHOÁCAN AT RISK; LIFE-THREATENING FLOODING AND MUDSLIDES
major_events.status: ACTIVE — Hurricane Simon peaked as a Category 4 storm with 155 mph (250 km/h) sustained winds off Mexico’s Pacific coast on Saturday 11 October, then weakened to Category 3 (127 mph / 205 km/h) by Sunday evening; the storm was centred approximately 45 miles south-southwest of Cabo Corrientes, Jalisco — the area the NHC assessed as most likely for a direct hit; President Claudia Sheinbaum urged residents of coastal Jalisco, Colima, Nayarit and Michoacán to remain sheltered; Jalisco suspended classes in 22 coastal municipalities and began evacuations; NHC forecast: system continues northwest before turning northeast across west-central Mexico mid-week, with Sinaloa potentially affected Wednesday–Thursday
major_events.impact: NHC forecast 10–20 inches of rainfall over Michoacán, Colima and Jalisco, with isolated totals to 30 inches producing life-threatening flooding and mudslides; class suspensions across 22 Jalisco coastal municipalities; evacuations underway in at-risk communities; tourist resort areas along the Jalisco Riviera (Puerto Vallarta corridor) facing strong winds, heavy rain and significant surf; no official damage or fatality reports confirmed yet; storm expected to cross Mexican interior by midweek then weaken over land

major_events.name: Tropical Storm Rachel (Eastern Pacific) — COASTAL FLOODING AND HIGH SURF SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA; TROPICAL STORM WATCH SAN DIEGO COUNTY THROUGH 13 OCT; FLASH FLOOD THREAT SOUTHERN CA TO ARIZONA/NEVADA
major_events.status: ACTIVE / WINDING DOWN — Tropical Storm Rachel targeted the California and northern Baja coast with flooding rain, high surf and tropical-storm-force winds beginning the weekend of 8–9 October; NWS issued a tropical storm watch for San Diego County running Friday evening through Tuesday 13 October, warning of 6–10 foot wave heights and heavy rain; a Level 2-of-4 flash flood threat extended from Southern California to Phoenix and Las Vegas as Rachel’s tropical moisture entrained into a jet-stream dip and spread northeast; a coastal flood warning covered LA and Orange County beaches through Sunday afternoon
major_events.impact: 6–10 ft wave heights along San Diego County and northern Baja coast; coastal flooding reported at LA and Orange County beaches; up to 2–3 inches rain forecast near Las Vegas and Phoenix; flash flood risk Level 2 across Southern California, Arizona and Nevada; California forecasters describe Rachel as a preview of Super El Niño-enhanced Pacific tropical incursions into Southern California; system expected to fully weaken as it interacts with land and cooler SSTs; final damage and rainfall totals pending

major_events.name: Hurricane Isaias — POST-TROPICAL RECOVERY; DEATH TOLL 4 (FL/AL); OUTAGES REDUCED ~330K (DOWN FROM 700K+); FPL TARGETS MONDAY NEAR-FULL RESTORATION; 17,000 WORKERS FROM 29 STATES; FEMA ACTIVE
major_events.status: RECOVERY UNDERWAY — Governor DeSantis confirmed recovery operations underway with roads clearing and businesses accessing emergency loans; Florida Power & Light reported approximately 332,000 customers remaining without power as of Sunday morning — down from 700,000+ immediately after landfall; FPL targets near-full restoration by end of day Monday 12 October; more than 17,000 utility workers from 29 states are actively assisting restoration efforts; electric cooperatives in hardest-hit Panhandle counties targeting Tuesday for full restoration; Florida activated approximately 5,000 National Guard members
major_events.impact: Death toll remains 4 (2 in Florida, 2 in Alabama); approximately 332,000–448,000 customers still without power Sunday morning (substantially reduced from 700,000+ post-landfall); FEMA disaster declarations active for Gulf Coast counties; roads cleared and debris removal ongoing; emergency business loans accessible; mutual-aid crews from central Florida utilities dispatched to Panhandle and Alabama; electric cooperative customers in DeFuniak Springs area targeted for Tuesday restoration; risk of river flooding diminishing

major_events.name: Typhoon Koguma (JTWC 27W) — WEAKENING; ~195 KM/H (~105 KT); EXPANDING STORM-FORCE WINDS EAST OF JAPAN; RECURVATURE NORTH-NORTHEAST UNDERWAY; EXTRATROPICAL TRANSITION IMMINENT
major_events.status: ACTIVE, WEAKENING — RECURVING — WeatherNews Japan’s update from late 11 October places Typhoon 29 (Koguma) with winds of approximately 195 km/h, down from the 222 km/h (120 kt) JTWC confirmed on 10 October; latest track positions the system approximately 1,161 km southeast of Yokosuka, moving north-northeastward; storm-force winds are expanding in radius as intensity decreases; extratropical transition is imminent as Koguma crosses cooler SSTs; no typhoon watches or warnings for mainland Japan or the Marianas
major_events.impact: Storm-force seas and heavy swell across the Ogasawara Islands and seas east of Honsū; elevated swell on east-facing Japan coasts through mid-week; port closures and elevated-wave risk for east-coast Japan shipping lanes; once extratropical, accelerating remnant low drives significant North Pacific swell; Japan Times notes this was the first time in five years three simultaneous October Northwest Pacific systems existed concurrently

major_events.name: Southeast Asian Haze — ONGOING; INDONESIA DEPLOYS 60,000 FIREFIGHTERS; PM ANWAR SPEAKS DIRECTLY WITH PRESIDENT PRABOWO; 288 HOTSPOTS CENTRAL KALIMANTAN; SCHOOL CLOSURES 2 MILLION STUDENTS
major_events.status: ONGOING — RESPONSE SCALED UP — Indonesia deployed 60,000 personnel to fight fires across Sumatra and Kalimantan as of 11 October, per an Indonesian minister at high-level bilateral talks with Malaysian counterparts; Malaysia Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim confirmed a direct call with Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto, who agreed to take “necessary steps”; school closures affecting approximately two million students across Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and several Malaysian states continued; hotspot counts remain elevated at 288 detected in Central Kalimantan; Singapore NEA continues to report air quality in the “very unhealthy” range
major_events.impact: 60,000 Indonesian firefighters deployed across Sumatra and Kalimantan; more than 200,000 hectares burned; more than 170,000 respiratory infection cases recorded by Indonesia’s Ministry of Health; school closures affecting approximately 2 million students in Malaysia; Singapore PSI at Very Unhealthy levels; haze extending to the Philippines; cloud seeding constrained by insufficient cloud formation; Malaysia continues to seek urgent ASEAN environment ministers’ meeting; bilateral Indonesia–Malaysia coordination now elevated to PM/presidential level

weather.overview_html: As of Monday 12 October, five simultaneous high-impact weather events demand attention. Hurricane Simon peaked as a Category 4 storm off Mexico’s Pacific coast and has weakened to Category 3, threatening Jalisco, Colima, Nayarit and Michoacán with life-threatening rainfall totals up to 30 inches. Tropical Storm Rachel continues to bring coastal flooding, high surf and flash flood risk across Southern California and into the Desert Southwest through Tuesday, with NWS maintaining a tropical storm watch for San Diego County. Hurricane Isaias’ recovery is advancing: FPL has reduced outages from 700,000+ to approximately 332,000 and targets near-full restoration today, with 17,000 workers from 29 states deployed. Typhoon Koguma is weakening to approximately 195 km/h as it recurves northeast over the open North Pacific with extratropical transition imminent. Indonesia has escalated its fire-suppression response to 60,000 deployed personnel as the SE Asian haze crisis enters its third week and Malaysia’s PM Anwar has spoken directly with President Prabowo.

items.source: Al Jazeera / CNN / NPR / PBS / CBC
items.headline: Hurricane Simon: Category 4 Peak (155 mph) Off Mexico’s Pacific Coast; Weakened to Cat-3 Sunday Evening; Threatening Jalisco, Colima, Nayarit, Michoacán; Up to 30” Rain Forecast; Classes Suspended 22 Municipalities
items.summary: Hurricane Simon peaked as a Category 4 hurricane with 155 mph (250 km/h) sustained winds off Mexico's Pacific coast on October 11, 2026, the most likely point for a direct hit being near Cabo Corrientes, Jalisco. By Sunday evening the storm had weakened to Category 3 with approximately 127 mph (205 km/h) sustained winds. President Claudia Sheinbaum urged residents of coastal Jalisco, Colima, Nayarit and Michoacán to remain sheltered. Jalisco state suspended classes in 22 coastal municipalities and began evacuating residents from at-risk areas. The NHC forecast life-threatening flooding and mudslides from rainfall totals of 10–20 inches broadly, with isolated amounts up to 30 inches in Michoacán, Colima and Jalisco. The storm was moving slowly — approximately 5 mph northwest — amplifying rainfall totals. Forecasters expected Simon to turn northeast and cross west-central Mexico midweek, with Sinaloa potentially affected Wednesday–Thursday before the system weakens over land.

items.source: NBC Palm Springs / Fox Weather / Times of San Diego
items.headline: Tropical Storm Rachel: Flooding Rain, 6–10 ft Surf and Tropical-Storm-Force Winds Hit Southern California; NWS Tropical Storm Watch San Diego County Through 13 Oct; Flash Flood Level 2 Threat Desert Southwest
items.summary: Tropical Storm Rachel brought coastal flooding, 6–10 foot wave heights, and tropical-storm-force winds to Southern California and northern Baja California beginning October 8–9, 2026. The National Weather Service issued a tropical storm watch for San Diego County from Friday evening through Tuesday October 13, warning of heavy rain, high winds, and significant surf. A coastal flood warning was in effect for LA and Orange County beaches through Sunday afternoon. Fox Weather reported a Level 2 of 4 flash flood threat from Southern California to Phoenix and Las Vegas, with up to 2–3 inches of rain forecast near those cities as Rachel's tropical moisture entrained into a jet-stream trough spreading northeast. California forecasters described the event as a preview of potentially enhanced Pacific tropical incursions into Southern California under the active 2026 Super El Niño. The system was expected to fully weaken as it interacted with land and cooler SSTs north of Baja.

items.source: CBS 12 / WFTV / ClickOrlando / DeSantis press office
items.headline: Hurricane Isaias Recovery: Outages Reduced to ~332,000 (Down from 700,000+); FPL Targets Near-Full Restoration Monday 12 Oct; 17,000 Workers from 29 States Deployed; 5,000 National Guard Activated; FEMA Active
items.summary: As of Sunday morning October 11, Florida Power & Light reported approximately 332,000 customers remaining without power — down from a peak of roughly 700,000– immediately after Isaias's landfall on Friday. FPL had restored more than 200,000 accounts and targeted near-full restoration by the end of Monday October 12. Governor DeSantis gave a recovery update confirming that major roads were clearing, debris removal was underway, and businesses were able to apply for emergency loans. The State of Florida activated approximately 5,000 National Guard members and more than 1,100 FDOT workers. More than 17,000 utility workers from 29 states were assisting restoration. Electric cooperatives serving hardest-hit rural Panhandle areas targeted Tuesday for full restoration; CHELCO lost about 90% of its system (68,900 customers). The death toll remains at four (two in Florida, two in Alabama).

items.source: WeatherNews Japan / Zoom Earth / AccuWeather / Japan Times
items.headline: Typhoon Koguma Weakens to ~195 km/h (~105 kt); Recurvature North-Northeast Underway; Storm-Force Winds Expanding East of Japan; Extratropical Transition Imminent; Japan Times Notes First Three-Simultaneous-October-System Event in Five Years
items.summary: WeatherNews Japan's late October 11 bulletin placed Typhoon 29 (Koguma) at approximately 195 km/h sustained winds, down from the 222 km/h (120 kt) JTWC confirmed at 12:00 UTC October 10. Zoom Earth's tracker placed the system approximately 1,161 km southeast of Yokosuka, moving northward at 19 km/h. Storm-force winds are expanding in radius as the storm recurves north-northeastward across the subtropical ridge axis. Extratropical transition is imminent; no typhoon watches or warnings are in effect for mainland Japan or the Marianas. AccuWeather described the system as approximately 627 miles from Yokosuka. The Japan Times reported that Koguma was the third concurrent Western Pacific tropical system in October — the first time in five years three systems coexisted in that month — a record context shaped in part by the 2026 Super El Niño's anomalously warm tropical Pacific SSTs.

items.headline: SE Asian Haze Day 11+: Indonesia Deploys 60,000 Firefighters Across Sumatra and Kalimantan; PM Anwar–President Prabowo Direct Call; 288 Hotspots Central Kalimantan; ~2 Million Students in School Closures
items.summary: Indonesia deployed 60,000 firefighting personnel across Sumatra and Kalimantan by October 11, 2026, according to a statement from an Indonesian minister at high-level bilateral talks with Malaysian counterparts. Malaysia Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim confirmed a direct conversation with Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto, who agreed to take 'necessary steps.' Ministry tally showed 288 hotspots in Central Kalimantan, followed by South Sumatra and West Kalimantan. School closures affecting approximately two million students across Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and several Malaysian states continued. Singapore's National Environment Agency continued to report air quality in the 'very unhealthy' range. Cloud seeding operations remained constrained by insufficient cloud formation. Malaysia continues to push for an urgent ASEAN environment ministers' meeting. Indonesia's Ministry of Health has recorded over 170,000 respiratory infection cases; more than 200,000 hectares have burned.

renewables.overview_html: Poland’s first offshore wind farm completed all 76 Vestas V236-15 MW turbine installations at Baltic Power on 7 October, entering final commissioning. India confirmed record-pace renewables additions: 35.2 GW of solar and 4.69 GW of wind in the first nine months of 2026, pushing cumulative solar capacity past 171 GW according to JMK Research and MNRE data published 8 October; Wood Mackenzie projects full-year solar additions above 50 GW. Sumitomo Corporation agreed a 49% stake in Hero Future Energies’ 500 MWp solar-wind-BESS hybrid in Karnataka (25-year PPA to SJVN; COD March 2027). On offshore wind, Norway revised its Utsira Nord floating-wind support terms while RWE divested a 33.33% stake in the consented 1.1 GW Five Estuaries (UK) project to EDF. On the utility-scale solar side, Grenergy closed US$460 million for 446 MW solar + 1.8 GWh storage in Chile and Clearway broke ground on the 650 MW Swan Energy Center in Missouri.

items.headline: India Adds 35.2 GW Solar and 4.69 GW Wind in First Nine Months of 2026; Cumulative Solar Exceeds 171 GW; Wood Mackenzie Projects Full-Year Solar Above 50 GW; Record Annual Pace Continues
items.summary: JMK Research and MNRE data published October 8, 2026 confirm India added 35.2 GW of solar and 4.69 GW of wind capacity in the first nine months of 2026 (January–September), bringing cumulative installed solar capacity above 171 GW. September alone contributed approximately 3.0 GW of solar additions. Wood Mackenzie projects full-year solar installations will exceed 50 GW, surpassing the prior year's record of approximately 49 GW. Solar installations represent the dominant share of India's total renewable additions, with solar accounting for around 56% of cumulative installed RE capacity. The pace puts India on track to meet and potentially exceed its interim renewable energy targets ahead of 2030 goals.

items.source: Sumitomo Corporation / PV Magazine India / Mercom India
items.headline: Sumitomo Corporation Acquires 49% Stake in Hero Future Energies’ 500 MWp Solar-Wind-BESS Hybrid Project in Bidar, Karnataka; 25-Year PPA to SJVN; 200 MWh Storage; Commercial Operations March 2027
items.summary: Sumitomo Corporation agreed on October 5, 2026 to acquire a 49% stake in Clean Solar Power (Baniyana) Pvt. Ltd., the project company for a ~500 MWp solar and wind hybrid project in Bidar, Karnataka being developed by Hero Future Energies (HFE). The project includes a co-located 200 MWh battery energy storage system. Power will be sold primarily to SJVN Limited under a 25-year power purchase agreement, with surplus traded on the energy exchange market. Commercial operations are targeted for March 2027. HFE retains 51% through its subsidiary Hero Solar Energy. Nomura served as financial advisor to HFE. Financial terms were not disclosed. HFE reports a global portfolio of 7.7 GWp of renewable energy assets and 2.9 GWh of BESS capacity across India, Ukraine, Vietnam and the UK.

items.source: OffshoreSource / Cadeler / OE Digital / Ocean News
items.headline: Baltic Power: Cadeler Completes All 76 Vestas V236-15 MW Turbine Installations at Poland’s First Offshore Wind Farm; 1.1–1.2 GW; Northland/Orlen JV; Full Commissioning Imminent; First Power July 2026
items.summary: Cadeler announced October 7, 2026 the completion of all 76 turbine installations at Baltic Power, Poland's first offshore wind farm, using jack-up vessels Wind Osprey and Wind Mover. Turbines are 76 Vestas V236-15 MW units; capacity is reported as 1.1–1.2 GW (Reuters 1.1 GW; trade media 1.2 GW). The farm is jointly owned by Northland Power and PKN Orlen under a 25-year contract-for-difference subsidy mechanism. Baltic Power delivered first power to Poland's national grid in July 2026, with more than one-third of turbines already generating. The project now enters final commissioning and grid integration.

items.headline: Norway Revises Utsira Nord Floating Wind Support Terms: Reduced Pre-FID Withdrawal Penalty, Earlier State Aid Payments; Total Cap Unchanged at NOK 35 Billion (~€3.3 Billion); Government Cites Immature Supply Chain
items.summary: Norway's government revised support terms for the Utsira Nord 500 MW floating wind project on October 9, 2026, disclosed via the 2027 state budget. Key changes: the financial penalty for withdrawing before a final investment decision is reduced; part of the state aid payments will be advanced earlier in the project lifecycle. The total support cap remains unchanged at NOK 35 billion (~€3.3 billion, 2025 prices). The government links revisions to increased uncertainty from the immature floating wind supply chain. Parliament is separately considering whether additional external quality assurance of the support scheme is needed before further state commitments.

items.headline: RWE Completes Sale of 33.33% Stake in Five Estuaries Offshore Wind (1.1 GW Consented, UK) to EDF; EDF Assumes Lead Developer Role; RWE Reinvests in Consented Pipeline; No Financial Terms Disclosed
items.summary: RWE completed the transfer of its 33.33% ownership stake in the Five Estuaries UK offshore wind project to EDF Power Solutions UK and Ireland on October 8, 2026. EDF will now lead the joint venture. Five Estuaries received development consent December 17, 2025; the project is consented at up to 79 turbines, maximum tip height 370 m, ~1.1 GW capacity, in the southern North Sea near the Galloper wind farm off Suffolk. RWE stated it will reinvest the proceeds into its existing portfolio of consented offshore wind projects. No financial terms were disclosed.

items.headline: Sonnedix Acquires 54 MW Italy Solar Portfolio from EOS ReNewable Infrastructure Fund II; Macchiareddu (46.5 MW, Sardinia) + Aprilia (7.5 MW, Lazio); Sonnedix Italian Operating Capacity Exceeds 1.3 GW
items.summary: Sonnedix acquired two solar PV assets in Italy totalling 54 MW from EOS ReNewable Infrastructure Fund II on October 7–8, 2026: Macchiareddu (46.5 MW) in Sardinia and Aprilia (7.5 MW) in Lazio, both financed by a European bank consortium. The acquisition lifts Sonnedix's operational Italian capacity above 1.3 GW, following a 194 MW EOS/Capital Dynamics portfolio in March 2026 and a 260 MW Tuscania battery storage portfolio in July 2026.

items.headline: Grenergy Closes ~US$460 Million Non-Recourse Financing for 446 MW Solar and 1.8 GWh Storage in Chile; BNP Paribas-Led Consortium; Algarrobal + Palmas Cluster; Largest Grenergy Project Financing
items.summary: Grenergy closed approximately US$460 million in non-recourse senior financing on October 9, 2026, covering the Algarrobal platform (fifth phase of Oasis de Atacama: 242 MW solar + 1.5 GWh BESS) and the Palmas cluster (21 DG solar projects: 204 MW solar + 289 MWh BESS) in Chile. BNP Paribas coordinated and underwrote, with BBVA, J.P. Morgan Chase, MUFG Bank, Santander and Bank of Nova Scotia participating. The transaction is Grenergy's largest single project financing, bringing its total Chilean non-recourse debt beyond US$2.4 billion.

items.headline: Clearway Energy Group Breaks Ground on 650 MW Swan Energy Center (Missouri) After Closing $1.5 Billion Financing; 20-Year Google PPA; CIBC/DNB/NAB Consortium; $80 Million PILOT for Local Schools; Target COD 2028
items.summary: Clearway Energy Group closed $1.5 billion in project financing and commenced construction on the 650 MW Swan Energy Center in Bates County, Missouri on October 7, 2026. Banking consortium: CIBC, DNB Bank and National Australia Bank. The project carries a 20-year PPA with Google, with Blattner Energy as construction partner (up to 500 peak jobs) and a 30-year PILOT generating more than $80 million for local schools and county services. Commercial operations targeted for 2028.

science.overview_html: A Nature Climate Change study published 6 October overturns a central assumption in biodiversity risk: climate-driven local extinctions are now occurring faster in temperate regions than in the tropics, driven by greater climate velocity at mid-latitudes. The WMO’s 8 October El Niño update — projecting a record-shattering Niño 3.4 anomaly of +3.7°C for December 2026 — delivers a new observational benchmark for the climate-variability community. On AI weather, Beucler et al.’s 13-author review of AI pathways from weather to climate identifies the explicit representation of external forcings as the critical gap preventing weather-forecast AI gains from extending to climate projection timescales. The Met Office–Turing FastNet physically-consistent GNN addresses the endemic front-blurring problem in data-driven models. A PNAS meta-analysis of 20,736 tipping-point papers exposes structural research-attention disparities: Greenland ice sheet at 20% of all papers versus permafrost abrupt thaw at only 0.7%.

items.headline: Nature Climate Change: Temperate Local Extinctions From Climate Change Are Outpacing Tropical Extinctions; Greater Climate Velocity at Mid-Latitudes Drives Faster Species Loss; Challenges Dominant Biodiversity-Risk Framing
items.summary: A Nature Climate Change study published October 6, 2026 reports that climate-driven local species extinctions (extirpations) are now occurring at a faster rate in temperate regions than in the tropics — an empirical reversal of the dominant paradigm that tropical biodiversity is the primary near-term casualty of warming. The authors attribute this to greater climate velocity in temperate zones under current rapid warming rates, which species with limited dispersal ability cannot track. The finding has direct implications for conservation policy in Europe, North America and East Asia, which have focused biodiversity protection resources disproportionately on tropical ecosystems.

items.headline: WMO October 2026 El Niño Monitoring Update: Niño 3.4 at +3.34°C Observed 6 Oct, Projected +3.7°C for OND — Would Be Strongest Since Records Began; Central Pacific First-Ever 30°C Reading; IOD Positive
items.summary: The WMO Global Seasonal Climate Update (October 7–8, 2026) reports the observed Niño 3.4 anomaly reached +3.34°C on October 6 and is projected to average +3.7°C for October–December 2026, peaking around December — far above the prior record of +2.6°C from November 2015. The central equatorial Pacific exceeded 30°C (86°F) for the first time in the continuous SST record. A positive Indian Ocean Dipole, peaking in October, combines with the El Niño forcing. The consensus of 13 national and international modelling centres gives near-100% probability of persistence through February 2027.

items.headline: Artificial Intelligence Pathways from Weather to Climate (arXiv:2610.09770, Beucler et al.): Explicit External Forcing Representation Required to Bridge Forecast and Climate Timescales; 13-Author Review Submitted to Science Advances
items.meta: Tom Beucler, David Neelin, Hui Su, Ignacio Lopez-Gomez, Chris Bretherton, Oliver Watt-Meyer, Tapio Schneider, Costa Christopoulos, Will Chapman, Laure Zanna, Aditya Grover, Adam Subel et al. (UNIL/UCLA/Google Research/Caltech/NYU/AI2/UC Boulder) · arXiv:2610.09770 (physics.ao-ph, cs.AI, cs.LG) · Submitted to Science Advances 7 October 2026
items.summary: Beucler et al. identify the critical gap between weather and climate AI: models must represent external forcings (greenhouse gases, aerosols, land-use change) explicitly before medium-range forecast gains can extend to climate projection skill. Two proposed diagnostic tests: (1) whether models treat external forcings explicitly; (2) whether models are robust out-of-distribution including extremes and counterfactual scenarios. Key finding: AI models are not intrinsically more efficient than GPU-ported dynamical models once architectural complexity is accounted for. Data-driven models have recently approached dynamical models on subseasonal timescales (~1 month) in probabilistic benchmarks.

items.headline: FastNet v1.0: Met Office–Turing GNN Embeds Physical Consistency Constraints During Training; Matches or Exceeds Met Office Global Model; Validated Against Hurricane Ian and Storm Ciarán; Addresses Front-Blurring Endemic to Data-Driven Models
items.meta: Met Office / Alan Turing Institute · arXiv:2509.17658 (physics.ao-ph) · Published October 2026
items.summary: FastNet v1.0 is a graph neural network embedding physical consistency constraints during training rather than as post-hoc corrections. It matches the Met Office Global Model on most metrics at tens of thousands of times the inference speed. Validation against Hurricane Ian (2022) and Storm Ciarán (2023) shows more realistic storm core structures and improved pressure–wind relationships — directly addressing the sharp-fronts blurring that remains an endemic problem in pure data-driven AI weather models.

items.headline: Nature Geoscience (Kopp et al.): Antarctic Ice Loss “Very Likely” on All 2100 Emissions Pathways; Highest-Ambition Paris Pathway Halves Upper-End SLR vs. Very High Emissions; 95th-Percentile Very High Emissions: 25.4 cm by 2100
items.meta: Robert Kopp et al. (Rutgers University RCEI) · Nature Geoscience · Published October 2026
items.summary: A Nature Geoscience study (Kopp et al., Rutgers) finds Antarctic ice loss contributing to global sea-level rise by 2100 is 'very likely' under all studied emissions scenarios. Under very high emissions, the 95th-percentile Antarctic SLR contribution reaches 25.4 cm by 2100 (median 15.7 cm). The highest-ambition Paris-consistent pathway carries at least 89% probability of producing less ice loss by century's end, reducing the upper-end contribution by roughly half. The authors stress the window for meaningful near-term emissions choices to bound long-term Antarctic SLR risk remains open despite committed ice loss being unavoidable.

items.headline: PNAS Meta-Analysis (20,736 Papers): Greenland Dominates Tipping Research (20%); Permafrost Abrupt Thaw Covered in Only 0.7%; Structural Scientific Attention Disparity May Skew Policy Prioritisation
items.summary: A PNAS meta-analysis of 20,736 publications on 14 climate tipping elements found the Greenland ice sheet appearing in 4,141 papers (20% of the dataset). By contrast, abrupt thaw of permafrost in boreal forests — identified as a major positive carbon-feedback risk — appeared in only 139 papers (0.7%). High-risk tipping elements including permafrost carbon feedback and West African monsoon shifts are substantially understudied relative to their potential climate impact, creating a potential structural bias in the evidence base informing climate policy.

items.source: VU Amsterdam / TU Delft / University of Amsterdam / EMS Annual Meeting 2026
items.headline: Xaurora: Probabilistic Generative Ensemble Forecasting via Stochastic Interpolants on Microsoft Aurora Foundation Model; Competitive with DLWP Ensembles at Fraction of Training Cost via LoRA Fine-Tuning
items.meta: VU Amsterdam, TU Delft, University of Amsterdam · EMS Annual Meeting 2026
items.summary: Xaurora converts Microsoft's deterministic Aurora foundation model into a fully generative stochastic ensemble system using the stochastic interpolant framework and LoRA fine-tuning. Results are competitive with state-of-the-art NWP ensembles and other data-driven approaches at a fraction of training cost, providing a practical pathway for converting any large pre-trained deterministic weather foundation model into a probabilistic ensemble system without full retraining.

items.title: Grenergy Closes ~US$460 Million Non-Recourse Senior Financing for 446 MW Solar + 1.8 GWh Storage Portfolio in Chile; BNP Paribas-Led Six-Bank Consortium; Largest Grenergy Project Financing; Chilean Total Debt Exceeds US$2.4 Billion
items.body_html: Grenergy closed approximately US$460 million in non-recourse senior financing on 9 October 2026 for the Algarrobal platform (fifth phase of Oasis de Atacama: 242 MW solar + 1.5 GWh BESS) and the Palmas cluster (21 DG projects: 204 MW solar + 289 MWh BESS) in Chile. BNP Paribas coordinated and underwrote; BBVA, J.P. Morgan Chase, MUFG Bank, Santander and Bank of Nova Scotia co-participated. The deal is Grenergy’s largest single project financing, bringing its total Chilean non-recourse debt beyond US$2.4 billion.

items.title: RWE Completes Sale of 33.33% Stake in Five Estuaries UK Offshore Wind (1.1 GW Consented) to EDF; EDF Assumes Lead Developer Role; RWE Reinvests Proceeds in Consented Pipeline; No Terms Disclosed
items.body_html: RWE Offshore Wind GmbH completed the transfer of its 33.33% stake in the Five Estuaries offshore wind project to EDF Power Solutions UK and Ireland on 8 October 2026. EDF will now lead the joint venture for the project (development consent December 2025; up to 79 turbines at ~1.1 GW, southern North Sea, extension of the Galloper wind farm off Suffolk). RWE stated proceeds will be reinvested in other consented offshore wind projects. Financial terms were not disclosed.

items.title: Sonnedix Acquires 54 MW Italy Solar Portfolio from EOS ReNewable Infrastructure Fund II (Macchiareddu, Sardinia + Aprilia, Lazio); Italian Operating Capacity Exceeds 1.3 GW; Third Italian Transaction in 2026
items.body_html: Sonnedix acquired two solar PV assets totalling 54 MW from EOS ReNewable Infrastructure Fund II on 7 October 2026: Macchiareddu (46.5 MW, Sardinia) and Aprilia (7.5 MW, Lazio), financed by a European bank consortium. The transaction lifts Sonnedix’s Italian operational portfolio above 1.3 GW — the company’s third Italian acquisition in 2026 (following a 194 MW portfolio in March and a 260 MW Tuscania battery storage portfolio in July).

items.title: Sumitomo Corporation Acquires 49% Stake in Hero Future Energies’ 500 MWp Solar-Wind-BESS Hybrid Project in Bidar, Karnataka (India); 25-Year PPA to SJVN; 200 MWh BESS; Commercial Operations March 2027; Nomura Adviser to HFE
items.body_html: Sumitomo Corporation agreed on 5 October 2026 to acquire a 49% stake in Clean Solar Power (Baniyana) Pvt. Ltd., the project company for a ~500 MWp solar and wind hybrid facility being developed by Hero Future Energies (HFE) in Bidar, Karnataka, India, co-located with a 200 MWh battery storage system. Power will be sold to SJVN Limited under a 25-year PPA with surplus marketed via the energy exchange; commercial operations are targeted for March 2027. Hero Future Energies retains 51% through its subsidiary Hero Solar Energy; Nomura acted as financial adviser to HFE. Financial terms were not disclosed. HFE reports a global portfolio of 7.7 GWp of renewable energy assets and 2.9 GWh of BESS capacity.
